name: TPS3831K33DQNR
title: TPS3831 and TPS3839: 150 nA single-rail voltage supervisors with push-pull active-low reset
summary: Two families of supply supervisors drawing 150 nA typical from the rail they watch. Each holds its push-pull RESET output low while VDD is under a factory-set threshold and for a 200 ms typical delay after VDD climbs back above threshold plus hysteresis; short dips on VDD are rejected. The TPS3831 adds an active-low manual reset input, MR, with an internal 20 kΩ pull-up; the TPS3839 has none. Operating supply is 0.9 V to 6.5 V and the output state is correct from VDD = 0.6 V. TPS3831K33DQNR is the TPS3831 with a 2.93 V threshold, for 3.3 V rails, in the 1 mm × 1 mm X2SON (DQN) on a 3000-piece reel.

circuits.title: Supervising a 3.3 V microprocessor
circuits.description: A TPS383xK33 sits on the processor's 3.3 V rail with C1, 0.1 µF, from VDD to ground. Its RESET output goes straight to the processor's RST input and keeps the processor in reset whenever the rail is under 2.93 V and for td after it recovers. On the TPS3831 a push button from MR to ground gives a manual reset; the TPS3839 has no MR pin.

circuits.title: MR driven through a logic-level FET
circuits.description: An n-channel logic-level FET, source to ground and drain on MR, pulls MR low when its gate is driven high and otherwise leaves MR to the internal 20 kΩ pull-up. It is used to keep supply current low when the signal that commands a manual reset does not swing fully to VDD.
notes: The 20 kΩ pull-up from MR to VDD is inside the TPS3831.

circuits.title: Boost converter switched off at the end of an alkaline cell
circuits.description: A single alkaline cell feeds both a TPS3839A09 and a TPS61261 boost converter that makes 3.3 V at 40 mA. The supervisor's RESET drives the converter's EN, so when the cell falls to 0.9 V, its end-of-discharge voltage, the converter is put into shutdown. Together the two draw 250 nA typical from the spent cell. The converter has a 4.7 µH inductor from the cell to L, 10 µF on its input and on its output, FB tied to VOUT and 5 kΩ from RI to ground.

circuits.title: Connection to a bidirectional reset pin
circuits.description: A processor whose RST pin is both an input and an output is fed from the TPS3839K33 RESET through a 47 kΩ series resistor, which limits the current when the supervisor and the processor drive the reset line at the same time. Both share the 3.3 V rail.

operation.text: The device watches its own VDD pin. When VDD falls under the negative-going threshold VIT-, RESET goes low (20 µs typical power-down delay). When VDD rises above VIT- + Vhys, RESET stays low for td, 200 ms typical, and then goes high. Fast transients on VDD are rejected.

On power-up the output is undefined until VDD reaches 0.6 V, then held low; it goes high td after VDD passes VIT- + Vhys. A dip below VIT- pulls RESET low, and it returns high td after VDD is back above VIT- + Vhys. Taking MR below 0.3VDD pulls RESET low; RESET returns high td after MR goes back above 0.7VDD.
Whether a dip on VDD causes a reset depends on both its width tW and its depth, measured from VIT- down to the bottom of the dip. Combinations above the transient rejection curve reset the device.

A logic low on MR (0.3 VDD) asserts RESET, letting a processor or any logic gate force a reset. When MR goes high again and VDD is above threshold, RESET is released after td. MR has a 20 kΩ internal pull-up to VDD and may be left open when unused. A drive signal that does not swing fully to VDD makes current flow in that pull-up; a logic-level FET pulling MR to ground avoids it.
RESET follows VDD compared with VIT-.
The RESET state is undefined and cannot be relied on.

operation.topic: Sampling current and the VDD capacitor
operation.text: The 150 nA average comes from sampling: the dc draw is about 100 nA, rising to about 15 µA for about 200 µs each time the input is sampled. From a high-impedance supply (trace resistance included) that current pulse can drop VDD enough to cause a false reset. A 0.1 µF capacitor close to VDD holds the average at 150 nA and reduces the effect of a high-impedance source.
When RESET drives a processor reset pin that is also an output, a resistor in series between them limits current while both drive the line; 47 kΩ is used with the TPS3839K33.
The 0.9 V threshold option and the low operating voltage suit monitoring a single alkaline cell.
Supply range is 0.9 V to 6.5 V. The source should be low impedance so the sampling current does not upset the threshold.

The VDD connection must carry 15 µA with little drop. If VDD sags too far during the sampling pulses, put 0.1 µF next to VDD. The SOT-23 layout example has pin 1 to ground, pin 2 out to the RESET flag, and pin 3 to the input supply with CVDD from that pad to ground.
The X2SON exposed pad is for mechanical stability and is soldered to ground or to copper that is left unconnected.
Evaluation modules TPS3831G33EVM-187 (SLVU774) and TPS3839K33EVM-112 (SLVU758); SPICE models for both devices.
